cohort: 134 cases of spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (SDCP) from the Canadian Cerebral Palsy Registry (CCPR) and 1950 controls from the Alberta Pregnancy Outcomes and Nutrition (APrON) study
finding: Antenatal risk factors (pregnancy complications, maternal disease, substance use) and perinatal risk factors (infections, Caesarean section, and perinatal adversity) are associated with an increased risk of spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (SDCP) in term-born children.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of SDCP in term-born children.
